subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The energy supplied during boiling is used to:
options: Increase the temperature of the liquid
Break the bonds between particles so they separate
questions.explain: Latent heat of vaporisation goes into separating the particles, not raising the temperature.

questions.q: Which equation correctly defines density?
questions.explain: Density ρ = m/V: mass divided by volume. Its standard unit is kg/m³.

questions.q: A solid object floats on water. What can you conclude about its density?
options: It is greater than the density of water
It is equal to the density of water
It has no density because it floats
It is less than the density of water
questions.explain: An object floats when its mean density is less than that of the fluid (water, 1000 kg/m³); denser objects sink.

questions.q: When ice melts to water, the mass of the substance:
questions.explain: Melting is a physical change and no particles are gained or lost, so mass is conserved.

questions.q: Evaporation can occur:
options: Only when a substance is frozen
From the surface of a liquid below its boiling point
questions.explain: Evaporation happens at the surface of a liquid at temperatures below the boiling point.

questions.q: If a sealed container of gas is heated, the pressure increases because the particles:
options: Move faster and hit the walls more often and harder
questions.explain: Heating gives the particles more kinetic energy, so they collide with the walls more frequently and with greater force.

questions.q: Two objects have the same mass but object A has a larger volume than object B. Which statement is correct?
questions.explain: For the same mass, the smaller volume gives the larger density (ρ = m/V). So object B, with the smaller volume, is denser.

questions.q: What is the name of the change of state when a liquid turns directly into a solid?
questions.explain: Liquid to solid is freezing (solidification). Gas to liquid is condensing; liquid to gas is evaporating/boiling.

questions.q: What causes the pressure of a gas on the walls of its container?
options: The particles sticking to the walls
The weight of the gas particles resting on the walls
Gas particles colliding with the walls and exerting a force
questions.explain: Gas pressure is caused by particles colliding with the container walls; each collision exerts a tiny force, and the total over the wall area gives the pressure.

questions.q: Which statement about the particle model is correct?
options: Particles in a liquid can move past one another but stay close together
Particles in a liquid are arranged in a fixed regular pattern
Particles in a gas vibrate about fixed positions
Particles in a solid are far apart
questions.explain: In a liquid the particles are close together but free to move and flow past each other.

questions.q: In the density required practical, how is the volume of a small irregular stone best measured?
options: By using a displacement (eureka) can or measuring cylinder to find the volume of water it displaces
By weighing it on a balance
By measuring its length with a ruler
questions.explain: An irregular solid has no simple shape, so its volume is found from the volume of water it displaces when fully submerged (using a measuring cylinder or displacement can).

questions.q: A liquid generally has a higher density than the same substance as a gas because:
options: It is at a higher temperature
Its particles are much closer together
questions.explain: In a liquid the particles are packed much closer together than in a gas, giving more mass per unit volume.

questions.q: Which quantity is calculated using density = mass / volume?
questions.explain: Density is defined as the mass of a substance divided by its volume.

questions.q: What is the name of the change of state from a gas to a liquid?
questions.explain: Condensation is when a gas cools and changes into a liquid.

questions.q: Gas pressure in a sealed container is caused by:
options: Particles colliding with the container walls
questions.explain: Gas pressure results from gas particles colliding with the walls of their container.

questions.q: In which state of matter are the particles regularly arranged, touching, and only vibrating about fixed positions?
questions.explain: In a solid the particles are in a fixed, regular arrangement, held closely together, vibrating about fixed positions, which is why solids keep their shape.

questions.q: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the energy needed to:
options: Raise the temperature of 1 kg by 1 degree Celsius
questions.explain: Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 degree Celsius.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas is heated in a sealed, rigid container (constant volume). What happens to the gas pressure?
options: It decreases because particles slow down
It stays the same because volume is fixed
It increases because particles move faster and hit the walls harder and more often
questions.explain: Heating increases the particles' speed, so they collide with the walls more frequently and with greater force. With volume fixed, this raises the pressure.

questions.q: While a pure substance is melting, its temperature:
questions.explain: During a change of state the temperature stays constant because energy goes into breaking bonds, not raising temperature.

questions.q: Why does a gas have a much lower density than the same substance as a solid?
options: Gas particles have more mass each
Mass is destroyed when a solid becomes a gas
The particles become lighter as a gas
The particles are much further apart in a gas, so the same mass fills a larger volume
questions.explain: Changing state does not change the number or mass of particles, but in a gas they are spread far apart, so the same mass occupies a far larger volume, giving a much lower density.

questions.q: Compared with the same substance as a solid, the particles in a gas have:
options: The same energy but a fixed shape
More energy and are much further apart
Less energy and are closer together
questions.explain: Gas particles have more kinetic energy and are far apart, moving quickly in random directions.

questions.q: According to kinetic theory, the temperature of a gas is related to:
options: The size of the container only
The average kinetic energy of its particles
questions.explain: The higher the temperature, the greater the average kinetic energy of the gas particles.
